hypothesis_or_artifact: H1 — ADR-019's rejection of the deadline extension
label: READ
claim_quote: *Amending the deadline to 2027-12-31 and continuing*: legitimate, outcome-blind, and nearly free in compute, and it was declined on what it purchases rather than on what it costs. An extension buys the **published 0.18** assumption only; at the **registered 0.09** assumption the minimum N exceeds 1,200, which at 20.8 admissible days per month arrives around 2031. A Stage B under the extension answers only whether the effect persists at its published magnitude, and a FAIL still cannot separate decay from absence, which is the distinction the registered assumption exists to draw.
evidence_summary: The reason ADR-019 gives for declining is the registered DEGRADED scope, verbatim (REGISTRATION.md:44-46; frozen in code as DEGRADED_SCOPE, section0.py:55-58). The registration pre-committed to that scope as its expected outcome and as an acceptable one: 'The Section 9 arithmetic and the decay evidence of Section 14 point to DEGRADED' (:74-75) and 'A DEGRADED here narrows a question rather than abandoning it, and a BLOCKED is a documented answer, not a failure of process' (:82-85), both stated before the census existed. The registered rationale for the 0.09 assumption (:347-356) is a rationale for reporting power at 0.09 beside 0.18, not for treating a 0.18-scope answer as worthless: Section 0's GO clause is the only place 0.09 is a bar, and GO was already eliminated on archive density (:863-867). The declined option cost zero dollars and ~33 requests/day (:1084-1085) against a 200/day registered flow cap (config.py:136) and a 220-request lifetime total (:1160).
recomputation: [from stored data and code] Using the repository's own projection arithmetic (scripts/power_gate.py:71,78-80: forward days = weekdays x printed_day_rate 333/336, added to achieved 11), I reproduced its published scenarios exactly — 88 by 2026-12-31, 152 forward-only and 163 all-cohorts by 2027-03-31 (matching power.json:114-116) — and extended them: N = 237 (E1's minimum, the figure the closure is explicitly stated against, REGISTRATION.md:1015) is reached 2027-07-14, and N = 300 on 2027-10-12. A 2027-12-31 extension therefore clears E1's minimum with 5.5 months to spare and the governing 300 with 2.5. Script: SCRATCH/work/agentA-ETF/power_recompute.py (date arithmetic block).
would_resolve: An amendment reconciling ADR-019's grounds for rejection with Section 0's registered expectation and DEGRADED scope — i.e. stating whether a published-magnitude answer was, or was not, the answer this registration set out to buy.
confidence_why: Both texts are in the same repository, one rejects the scope the other registered in advance as its expected outcome, and the registered expectation predates any data.
invalidation_note: ADR-019 is in the final commit and ADR-020 supersedes only its collection consequence (DECISIONS.md:574).
disclosure_ref: Partial adjacent disclosure only: ETFExperiment/DECISIONS.md:551-553 discloses that the extension was legitimate, outcome-blind and nearly free and that it was declined on what it purchases. The record nowhere discloses that what it purchases is the registration's own pre-registered expected outcome, which is what this finding rests on, so the S3 disclosure cap does not apply.

hypothesis_or_artifact: H1 — the 'deadline finding' that carries the closure, and the closure kind untestable-at-achievable-power
label: DERIVED
claim_quote: **H1 closes at `untestable-at-achievable-power`.** The registered design cannot resolve the effect at the sample size reachable by the registered deadline of 2027-03-31.
evidence_summary: The word 'deadline' does not occur anywhere in the pre-registration proper: awk 'NR<=595 && /deadline/' over REGISTRATION.md (Sections 0-14 end at line 589, the amendment log opens at 591) returns nothing. The date 2027-03-31 occurs exactly three times before the amendments (:36, :48, :78) and in all three it is the horizon over which the achievable admissible-day count is computed, never a date by which anything must finish. The code names it a horizon: projection_deadline (config.py:89, set at :176 beside interim_deadline at :175), consumed only in Section 0 rationale strings (section0.py:130,:145) and by the projection in power_gate.py:73. Section 10's Stage B trigger carries no date at all (:394-398). The one registered rule that uses 2027-03-31 is the BLOCKED power trigger (:47-48), measured at 0.6105 (n = 163) and it did not fire (power.json:62; REGISTRATION.md:869-871); report.md:369-370 says so plainly. HYPOTHESES.md:48-49 defines the closure kind against 'the registered deadline', so the kind rests on a constraint the registration did not impose on itself.
recomputation: Minimum detectable rank correlation at 80 % power, alpha_adj one-sided, normal approximation to the permutation null (r*sqrt(n-1) ~ N(rho*sqrt(n-1), 1-rho^2)); inputs alpha_adj from src/etf/config.py:25 and N from reports/stage_a2/power.json:116. At N = 163 the MDE is rho = 0.218; at N = 237, rho = 0.181; at N = 300, rho = 0.161. At the projected count the design detects an effect 21 % larger than the published magnitude at 80 % power and reaches 61 % power against the published magnitude itself — a narrowed design, not an unresolvable one, on the registration's own 0.50/0.80 scale. Script: SCRATCH/work/agentA-ETF/power_recompute.py.
would_resolve: Point to a line in Sections 0-14 registering 2027-03-31 as a termination date rather than a projection horizon; failing that, an amendment recording that the stopping rule was created at closure time and stating why that is not a post-hoc bar.
confidence_why: HIGH for the textual claim, since the greps are exhaustive over the pre-registration; MEDIUM for the inference that the closure is premature, because an operator may stop a project for reasons outside its registration — but then the closure is an operator preference, not the registered untestable-at-achievable-power finding it is typed as.
invalidation_note: The amendment log is append-only and 4d11002 is final.
disclosure_ref: Partial adjacent disclosure only: ETFExperiment/report.md:369-370 discloses that the BLOCKED floor is cleared and that 'the registered deadline is what is not met', and ETFExperiment/DECISIONS.md:551 speaks of 'amending the deadline', presupposing one exists. hypothesis_or_artifact: H1 — reopen path (a), and the revision-integrity measurement dropped at Amendment 6
label: READ
claim_quote: **(a)** A flow source serving a **per-row publication timestamp**. Measured: **0 of 2** surviving sources serve one, and none documents a publication time. This removes the dependence on this repository's own capture cadence entirely and would make the full **333-day** out-of-sample series admissible in a single pass, clearing every minimum on the record at once.
evidence_summary: A per-row publication timestamp establishes when a row was published, not what value stood at that time, and the registered admissibility rule turns on the second: the as-printed value is 'the one in that capture' and a later value 'is never substituted' (REGISTRATION.md:155-158; ADR-002, DECISIONS.md:57-61). Reading today's value for a past row, with a timestamp attesting the row's age, is exactly that substitution unless the source's revision rate is known to leave sign and threshold intact. That revision rate is the measurement Amendment 6 dropped (REGISTRATION.md:1141, :1149), and the same amendment bars the only substitute: a future flow hypothesis 'must measure it from scratch and may not cite the n = 11 figure as evidence of anything' (:1152-1153; DECISIONS.md:608-611). So reopen (a), described as clearing 'every minimum on the record at once', cannot be exercised without redoing from scratch the 15-trading-day measurement the closure declined to finish, while the closure's own valuation table records path (a) as 'Does not need etf-snap' (:1125) — true of the collector, false of the measurement. The retro corroboration that would have carried the point is 0 revised / 0 sign flips / 0 threshold crosses on n = 11 against a registered minimum of 30 (retro_revision.json:3,:7-9; config.py:187) and is correctly refused as evidence (:889-895).
would_resolve: Restate reopen (a) as a conjunction — a per-row publication timestamp AND a revision-integrity measurement at the registered n >= 30 — or record that (a) implicitly assumes the revision rate the repository chose not to measure.
confidence_why: A source serving both a publication timestamp and an as-printed value history would satisfy (a) as written, but no such source is named and the two surviving sources serve neither (docs/ACCESS.md:104, :169).
invalidation_note: Amendment 6 is the final amendment and 4d11002 is the final commit.

hypothesis_or_artifact: H1 — the entry anchor amendment, and the finality of the admissibility count
label: DERIVED
claim_quote: If the measured **95th percentile first-print time falls later than 07:00 UTC**, the anchor moves to **the next whole hour after that percentile**, recorded by amendment **before any outcome read and before any admissibility count is final**.
evidence_summary: The measurement that may move the anchor never existed: the registration requires 15 US trading days of forward capture before any lag figure and 2 captures exist (progress.md:452-453). The admissibility count was nevertheless produced, treated as final and used to close: 336 rows / 11 admissible (census.json:1-2), carried into the power gate as achieved N (power_gate.py:65), into Amendment 3's power table (REGISTRATION.md:848-851) and into the closing figures (:1010-1015). The rule moves the anchor in one direction only, later (anchor.py:70-82), and a later anchor can only admit captures an earlier one excluded; 53 out-of-sample days are excluded as capture_too_late at the provisional anchor (census.json exclusion_reasons; archive_density.json:120). The repository's own retro evidence puts the print between +04:05 and +08:00 on D+1 with served-value captures (n = 11) at +07:11, +07:12, +07:16 x3 and +07:59:43 (ACCESS.md:413-414), a distribution whose 95th percentile plausibly sits past the 07:00 trigger. The archive-density function has no anchor parameter at all (archive.py:90-95), so every density and census figure is conditioned on the un-amended anchor with no sensitivity stated.
recomputation: Anchor sensitivity of the timemap-admissible count, recomputed from the raw untracked timemaps (live data/access/timemap-recent.txt and timemap-all_data.txt, read 2026-09-03T19:40Z, UNANCHORED) with the window [20:00 UTC on D, anchor on D+1) exactly as src/etf/archive.py:90-95 defines it, over the same n = 333-day universe: 08:00 anchor -> 37 admissible days (share 0.1111), 53 capture_too_late; 09:00 -> 40 (0.1201), 52; 10:00 -> 43 (0.1291), 52; 12:00 -> 48 (0.1441), 50; 14:00 -> 56 (0.1682), 48. The 08:00 row reproduces the repository's published figures exactly. The effect is real but bounded: at a 09:00 anchor achieved N would plausibly be 13-15 rather than 11 and the projected 163 would become roughly 165-167; no anchor the rule could produce restores the 0.60 density bar. Script: SCRATCH/work/agentA-ETF/anchor_sensitivity.py.
would_resolve: Either record the anchor amendment as forgone with a stated sensitivity band on every anchor-dependent figure, or note that the closure's admissibility count was declared final in advance of a registered step whose direction is known.
confidence_why: HIGH that the registered ordering was not followed, and HIGH that the magnitude is small (the recomputed sensitivity table bounds it at roughly +2 to +4 admissible days), which is why this is S3 and not higher.
invalidation_note: 4d11002 is final and the collector that would have supplied the first-print distribution was disarmed in it.
disclosure_ref: Partial adjacent disclosure only: ADR-001's Consequences (ETFExperiment/DECISIONS.md:39-42) discloses that the print lands between roughly 04:00 and 08:00 UTC and 'therefore that the anchor may well move. It has not moved and will not move on that evidence.' The record does not state that a final admissibility count was nonetheless produced and used to close, nor give any sensitivity to the anchor, which is what this finding rests on.
